subject: Escalation matrix and evidence custody: request for clarity on export windows
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Amir Qureshi <security@bluepeakhealth.com>, elaine.cho@bluepeakhealth.com
Date: 2028-04-05T08:14:00-04:00
Subject: Escalation matrix and evidence custody: request for clarity on export windows

Team —

BluePeak reached out this morning reporting a suspicious access pattern affecting a subset of patient metadata stored in our managed embeddings for their tenant (ticket: BLUE-4938). They flagged possible lateral access from an IP not associated with their org.

Before we commit to an evidence handoff, legal/ops needs clarity on a few DPA-related items so we can answer BluePeak precisely. I tried to summarize below — please reply inline where you can: 

1) Notification windows: our DPA references a "best-effort" notification and then an explicit 72-hour escalation for incidents that meet the confidentiality/availability threshold. For potential exposures that are low-confidence (suspicious access only), do we treat the 72-hour clock from initial detection or from confirmed scope? I need the exact position to provide to their counsel.

2) Evidence custody and export window: BluePeak is asking for a 90-day forensic access window and an option to retrieve forensic snapshots. Our standard position has been: provide a 30-day secure export and then extend via a signed SOP for longer periods. Can someone confirm if we have precedent for 90-day custody (esp. for EU customers)?

3) Subprocessor involvement: if we need to export storage-level logs or raw object stores, CloudHeap (our storage subprocessor in eu-west-1) will be involved. What is the minimal notice/authorization we require before transferring a snapshot that may cross borders? Any existing signed clauses with CloudHeap that would speed this up?

4) Transfer method and manifest: BluePeak prefers an integrity-signed manifest + SFTP with MFA. Are we comfortable agreeing to SFTP + manifest + signed chain-of-custody? Any operations obstacles?

5) Liaison matrix: I have drafted a minimal liaison matrix but want ops/legal to confirm roles — who is the formal Redwood point for forensic intake, who signs the transfer manifest, and who owns the billing/credits decision should we offer credits while we investigate?

Attached: incident_summary_v1.pdf (high-level detection log).

I want to respond with a short, concrete plan before EOD. Thanks —

— Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Head of Privacy & Risk, Redwood Inference
mailto:tessa.morgan@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0148
From: Amir Qureshi <security@bluepeakhealth.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-04-05T09:03:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Escalation matrix and evidence custody: request for clarity on export windows

Tessa —

Thanks for the quick heads up and for including our security team. A few clarifications from our side: 

- We view the 72-hour notification as triggered from first detection that meets the DPA's incident threshold. If Redwood's initial triage indicates credible unauthorized access to BluePeak data, we expect notification within that window. If it's low confidence, please state that in the notice but continue escalation if evidence grows.

- BluePeak legal prefers a 90-day forensic access window by default for anything involving patient-adjacent metadata. We're willing to sign an access agreement but want the export mechanism and custody process documented (manifest, hash, transfer logs).

- For cross-border transfers: our data protection officer requires prior listing of subprocessors that will handle raw exports and, for any non-EEA transfer, Standard Contractual Clauses or an equivalent legal basis.

- Transfer method: SFTP with an integrity-signed manifest is acceptable. For larger forensic snapshots we can accept a pre-signed encrypted object in our custody account (if Redwood can upload there).

If you can provide the liaison matrix and a short SOP for the first 30 days, we can review and provide comments. We can also schedule a 30-minute call this afternoon (14:00 CEST) if that helps.

— Amir Qureshi
Head of Security, BluePeak Health
security@bluepeakhealth.com
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Amir Qureshi <security@bluepeakhealth.com>
Date: 2028-04-05T11:08:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Escalation matrix and evidence custody: request for clarity on export windows

Tessa / Team —

Quick operational answers while legal weighs in: 

- 72-hour clock: we will treat "credible unauthorized access" as the trigger. Our triage notes (attached) show anomalous access markers but not confirmed exfil; I recommend we notify BluePeak now as "initial detection" with a pending update once full scope is known. That meets the DPA timeline and buys us time to contain.

- Evidence export window: engineering can produce a signed snapshot and hashes. We have historically offered a 30-day secure export by default; for enterprise/regulatory customers we've accommodated 90-day custody when requested and approved by Legal + Ops. If Legal flags no blockers, Ops can support 90 days — we will need a signed access agreement and an approved SFTP endpoint.

- Subprocessor (CloudHeap): they are contractually obligated to assist with exports but require a 48-hour notice to provision a support package for object-level retrieval in eu-west-1. 

- Transfer method: attached is a short runbook (evidence_export_instructions.md) describing manifest format, hashing (SHA-256), and SFTP posture. Ops can run a dry-run to the BluePeak endpoint today.

Proposed immediate next steps:
1) Tessa to send formal initial notification to BluePeak (we draft).
2) Ops (Ben) to initiate a dry-run export ready by EOD if BluePeak confirms an endpoint.
3) Legal (Kimberly) to confirm whether 90-day custody is acceptable as a standard response for this account and document any special clauses needed for CloudHeap involvement.

I can host the dry-run and produce the transfer manifest.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Security & Reliability Liaison, Redwood Inference
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Amir Qureshi <security@bluepeakhealth.com>, elaine.cho@bluepeakhealth.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-04-05T16:22:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Escalation matrix and evidence custody: request for clarity on export windows

Amir / Elaine —

Thanks for the clear guidance. Short plan from Redwood below; we'll send a formal notice (DPA-trigger) in parallel to legal counsel: 

1) Notification: Redwood will send an initial DPA notice now indicating "initial detection" (meets 72-hour best-effort window). We'll follow up with a scope confirmation within 48 hours once triage completes.

2) Evidence custody: Redwood Ops will prepare a signed snapshot and SHA-256 manifest. Ops can support a 90-day custodial access period for BluePeak pending execution of a short access agreement. If BluePeak prefers, we can also upload an encrypted object to a BluePeak-managed bucket (requires BluePeak to provide an upload target).

3) Subprocessor & cross-border: CloudHeap will be used for object retrieval in eu-west-1. Per existing contracts, CloudHeap requires 48 hours' notice to engage export tools. Any transfer outside the EEA will require SCCs; legal (Kimberly) will include the appropriate contractual basis in the access agreement.

4) Liaison matrix (roles):
- Forensic intake & export execution: Ben Carter (ben.carter@redwood.ai)
- Legal counsel / access agreement: Kimberly Park (kimberly.park@redwood.ai)
- Customer comms & policy: Tessa Morgan (tessa.morgan@redwood.ai)
- Ops point / manifest signer: Laura Bennett (laura.bennett@redwood.ai)

5) Transfer method: we'll attempt an SFTP dry-run today. Transfer will include: snapshot.tar.enc, snapshot.tar.enc.sha256, manifest.json (signed), and an operations chain-of-custody PDF.

Next actions:
- Amir, can you confirm the preferred target (SFTP endpoint or a BluePeak bucket) and whether BluePeak requires an independent integrity provider for the manifest?
- Kimberly, if you can draft the short access agreement (30/90-day options) I will loop BluePeak legal.

Attaching a liaison_matrix_v1.xlsx for your review. We'll schedule the 14:00 CEST call if that works for your team.

— Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Head of Privacy & Risk, Redwood Inference
